title: Why you can want and not want the same thing

unit.title: Why you can want and not want the same thing
unit.needIt: When you feel torn, it is not weakness or confusion. Minds have parts, and knowing which part is talking helps you decide which to follow.
unit.why: The lecture explores how humans are often conflicted inside. It uses stories like a man tempted by a sight he finds gross, a woman lost in a love she knows is wrong, and a man with a brain injury who could no longer control his impulses. These stories show that we are not just one single voice, but a mix of drives, instincts, and reasons.
unit.outcome: Identify the different internal forces that influence your choices and behaviors.
unit.reachesYou: You feel this when you want to scroll on your phone but know you should be sleeping. You see it when you choose a snack even though you promised yourself you would eat healthy.
unit.do: Notice one time today when you feel a 'tug' between what you want to do right now and what you know is better for you. Just observe the feeling without judging it.

quiz.q: What does Plato's story of Leontius show?
choices: A man who is perfectly calm
A man who hates his city
A man who is very brave
A man struggling with his own desires
quiz.why: Leontius felt a desire to look at something but was also disgusted by it.
quiz.quote: He had, says Socrates using Plato's terminology of appetite, he had an appetite to look at them, but at the same time he was disgusted and turned away.

quiz.q: How does Medea feel about her love for Jason?
choices: She loves him and wants nothing else
She is angry at him
She is happy with her choice
She thinks it is a mistake but cannot stop
quiz.why: Medea knows the love is against her better judgment but feels overtaken by a force.
quiz.quote: Meanwhile Medea, seized with fierce desire by reason, strives to quench the raging fire, but strives in vain.

quiz.q: What is the role of the 'ego' in Freud's theory?
choices: The source of all desires
The part that follows social norms
The part that controls the id
A part sensitive to reality
quiz.why: Freud describes the ego as the part of the self that is sensitive to reality and recognizes what is possible.
quiz.quote: The one, which he calls the ego, is a part of the self that is sensitive to reality.

choices: The relation between reason and drives
A circus act
How we control our bodies
How to train a pet
quiz.why: The rider represents the part of us with conscious control, while the elephant represents our drives.
quiz.quote: Haidt's first distinction is between what he calls mind and body.

quiz.q: What is 'confabulation' in the brain study?
choices: A type of memory loss
A way to speak two languages
Making up an explanation for an action
A physical injury
quiz.why: The man made up a reason for his actions because his brain's language center did not have the information.
quiz.quote: He comes up with an explanation for why it is that he has chosen as he has chosen.

quiz.q: How does the 'old brain' differ from the 'new brain'?
choices: It is faster than the new brain
It is shared with non-human animals
It is located only in the head
It is responsible for language
quiz.why: Haidt explains that the old brain is the part we share with non-human animals.
quiz.quote: Roughly, the parts of our brain, the brain stem and the subcortical regions, that we share with non-human animals

quiz.q: What happened to Phineas Gage's brain?
choices: It damaged his prefrontal cortex
It was a small scratch
It did not hurt him at all
It made him smarter
quiz.why: The damage to his prefrontal cortex caused him to lose his ability to self-regulate.
quiz.quote: In reconstructing the accident, it's become clear that the damage which the pole did was to an area of Gage's called the ventromedial prefrontal cortex.

partials: We often feel conflicted within ourselves.
Some drives are unconscious and hard to control.
Reason can be overridden by intense desires.
The prefrontal cortex helps us regulate our actions.
We can train ourselves through associations.
crystal.key: Human nature involves a constant internal conflict between different parts of the soul.

decoys.text: Reason is always in total control of our actions.
decoys.why: The lecture shows that reason is often overridden by appetite or instinct.

decoys.text: We are only one single, unified personality.
decoys.why: The lecture argues we are a bundle of different drives and parts.

crystal.aha: By understanding our internal divisions, we can better navigate the conflicts between our desires and our reason.
